title: Pork Egg Roll Bowls
subtitle: everything inside an egg roll, stir-fried in one pan: ground pork, cabbage and carrot in a ginger-soy sauce over rice
imageAlt: Stir-fried ground pork with shredded cabbage and carrot over rice in a white bowl on a navy napkin
servingsNote: dinner for one big eater + one hungry eater, plus 2 lunches

breakdown: Soy, rice vinegar, sesame oil, brown sugar

beforeYouStart.text: Start the rice first; the stir-fry is done in 15 minutes.
Use your biggest skillet or a wok; 2 bags of coleslaw mix look like a lot but cook down by half.

steps.title: Start the rice
steps.text: Rinse the rice until the water runs mostly clear. Bring it to a boil with the water and a pinch of salt, cover and simmer on low 15 minutes, then rest 10 minutes off the heat with the lid on. Fluff with a fork.

steps.title: Sauce
steps.text: Stir the soy sauce, vinegar, brown sugar and sesame oil together.

steps.title: Brown the pork
steps.text: Heat the oil in a large skillet or wok over medium-high. Cook the pork and onion, breaking up the pork, 8–10 minutes until browned and no pink remains (71°C / 160°F). Spoon off any fat.

steps.title: Aromatics
steps.text: Add the garlic and ginger and stir 30 seconds.

steps.title: Cabbage
steps.text: Add the coleslaw mix and the sauce and stir-fry 4–5 minutes, until the cabbage is tender-crisp.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Taste for soy and serve over the rice.

fixIt.fix: Keep the heat high and cook a minute or two longer, uncovered, so the cabbage juices evaporate.
Take it off while it still has some crunch; it keeps softening off the heat.
Add another splash of soy and a little more vinegar at the end.

saleTip: Coleslaw mix is often 2 for $4 at No Frills; a small green cabbage shredded at home is cheaper still.
swap: Ground chicken or turkey: same method, cooked to 74°C (165°F).
leftovers: Great for lunches; keep the rice separate so it doesn't go soggy.
doneness: Ground pork cooked to 71°C (160°F) with no pink (Health Canada). Reheat to 74°C (165°F).
source: Based on tested 'egg roll in a bowl' methods (Budget Bytes, Canadian Living): browned ground pork, ginger and garlic, coleslaw mix stir-fried in a soy-sesame sauce.
prepAhead: Mix the sauce and slice the onion up to 1 day ahead.
reheat: Covered in the microwave 2 minutes, stirring halfway, until 74°C (165°F).

basic.note: Pork, cabbage and soy sauce; no fresh ginger or vinegar.

stepNotes.1: Basic: soy sauce and brown sugar only.

fancy.note: Crispy wonton strips on top and a sweet plum dip, like the real thing.

addSteps.title: Wonton crisps
addSteps.text: Heat the oil in a small skillet over medium-high and fry the wonton strips in batches 30–60 seconds, until golden. Drain on paper towel and pile on the bowls, with plum sauce to drizzle.

plating: Rice on the bottom, stir-fry piled on top.
Plum sauce drizzled in a zigzag.

why.0-5: Bagged coleslaw mix is already shredded cabbage and carrot; no chopping.
why.0-4: Fresh ginger and garlic are what make it taste like an egg roll filling.
why.1-3: Sesame oil added at the end keeps its toasty flavour.

funFact: Egg rolls are a Chinese-American invention from the 1930s, thicker and crunchier than Chinese spring rolls.

keeps.note: the cabbage goes watery when thawed
